Útoky na saúdská ropná zařízení a metropoli Riad podtrhují selhání regionálního odstrašení a hrozbu nových výpadků dodávek energií.
assessment.security_status_en: The conflict in the Red Sea and Yemen has escalated sharply following a lightning Houthi offensive seizing Yemen's west coast and the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and Riyadh highlight failing regional deterrence and the ongoing threat of major energy supply disruptions.

recommendations.reason_cs: Uzavření klíčových bodů v Rudém moři nutí lodní přepravce k delším trasám kolem Afriky, což udržuje vysoké sazby za přepravu. Firmy z tohoto sektoru těží z vyšších marží navzdory geopolitickým rizikům.
recommendations.reason_en: The closure of key Red Sea chokepoints forces carriers to take longer routes around Africa, maintaining elevated freight rates. Shipping firms benefit from higher profit margins despite geopolitical risks.

recommendations.sector_cs: Obranný průmysl (např. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)
recommendations.sector_en: Defense Industry (e.g. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)
recommendations.reason_cs: Masivní schválené dodávky zbraní a munice pro Blízký východ a rostoucí napětí zajišťují dlouhodobý přísun lukrativních vládních zakázek. Poptávka po protiraketové obraně a přesné munici zůstává na rekordní úrovni.
recommendations.reason_en: Massive approved arms and ammunition packages for the Middle East and rising tensions ensure a steady flow of lucrative government contracts. Demand for missile defense and precision munitions remains at record highs.

recommendations.sector_cs: Ropa a Plyn (např. Shell, BP, Chevron)
recommendations.reason_cs: Poškození saúdských ropných infrastruktur a rostoucí napětí v okolí Hormuzského průlivu tlačí ceny energií vzhůru. Ropní giganti realizují nadstandardní zisky díky rostoucím cenám komodit.
recommendations.reason_en: Damage to Saudi oil infrastructure and rising tensions around the Strait of Hormuz are driving energy prices higher. Oil majors are generating outsized profits amid surging commodity prices.

recommendations.sector_cs: Evropský Spotřební sektor & Autoprůmysl (např. Volvo, BMW)
recommendations.reason_cs: Vysoké ceny pohonných hmot a rostoucí inflace silně zatěžují spotřebitelskou poptávku a marže automobilek. Narušení dodavatelských řetězců navíc zvyšuje provozní náklady.
recommendations.reason_en: High fuel prices and rising inflation heavily weigh on consumer demand and automotive margins. Furthermore, supply chain disruptions increase operational costs.

recommendations.sector_cs: Pražská burza: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.sector_en: Prague Stock Exchange: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.reason_cs: Domácí banky a energetika čelí globální makroekonomické nejistotě a inflačním tlakům spojeným s energetickou krizí. Trh zůstává v defenzivním módu bez výrazných růstových katalyzátorů.
recommendations.reason_en: Domestic banks and utilities face global macroeconomic uncertainty and inflationary pressures driven by the energy crisis. The market remains in a defensive posture without strong growth catalysts.

recommendations.sector_cs: Evropské blue-chips (např. Airbus, TotalEnergies, Allianz, Rheinmetall)
recommendations.sector_en: European blue-chips (e.g. Airbus, TotalEnergies, Allianz, Rheinmetall)
recommendations.reason_cs: Zatímco energetické a zbrojní tituly těží z konfliktu, širší evropský trh je zatížen makroekonomickou nestabilitou a nejistotou ohledně dodávek energií. Doporučuje se selektivní přístup zaměřený na defenzivní sektory.
recommendations.reason_en: While energy and defense stocks benefit from the conflict, the broader European market is burdened by macroeconomic instability and energy supply uncertainty. A selective approach focusing on defensive sectors is advised.

assessment.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další diplomatické manévry a hrozbu odvetných vojenských útoků USA a spojenců v reakci na houthiské útoky na Riad. Ceny ropy a tržní volatilita zůstanou na zvýšených úrovních kvůli obavám z širší regionální války.
assessment.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further diplomatic maneuvers and the threat of retaliatory military strikes by the US and allies are expected in response to Houthi attacks on Riyadh. Oil prices and market volatility will remain elevated due to fears of a broader regional war.
assessment.forecast_review_cs: Předchozí předpověď se částečně potvrdila, neboť eskalace konfliktů a hrozba amerických zásahů nadále drží ceny ropy a volatilitu na vysokých úrovních.
assessment.forecast_review_en: The previous forecast was partially confirmed, as escalating conflicts and threats of US interventions continue to keep oil prices and market volatility at high levels.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis are upending the Gulf order. The Saudis are the biggest losers
articles.summary:
Yemen's Houthis are upending the Gulf order. The Saudis are the biggest losers

Submitted by Joe Gill on Fri, 09/18/2026 - 20:05
The war has entered a critical phase, with the Iran-aligned group calling the shots, as Trump leaves Mohammed bin Salman out in the cold
Houthi supporters carry a portrait of the leader of the group, Abdul Malik al-Houthi, in a protest denouncing Saudi Arabia’s aggression against Yemen, in Sanaa, on 18 September 2026 (Mohammed Huwais/AFP)
Off

A ballistic missile strike hits a fuel depot close to Riyadh’s international airport. Air raid sirens wailed across the Saudi capital before dawn on Saturday, as they did across other regions, including Jeddah, Taif and Yanbu.

The Houthi strikes exposed how vulnerable the Gulf kingdom is to the Yemeni group’s recent wave of attacks on the country, which they say are a response to Saudi strikes on Yemen. 

Will US President Donald Trump assist his friend Mohammed bin Salman? The crown prince - who the US president failed to help when oil terminals were hit by missiles from Iraq in 2019 - called the White House asking for US support in its war with Ansar Allah (Houthis). Once again, Trump said no.

The $600bn that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman committed to investing in the US in his deals with Trump last year has bought almost zero protection from the world’s military superpower.

The administration offered to share intelligence and assist Riyadh with targeting operations, but Trump desperately wants to avoid opening any new fronts, with US forces overstretched in the blockade of Iran.

Instead, Trump made a deal with the group that had fought the Saudi coalition to a standstill in Yemen after a devastating eight-year war. Under the terms recently agreed in Muscat, Houthi leaders confirmed they would uphold a 2025 ceasefire with the US, ensuring the Red Sea remains open to global shipping, except for Saudi vessels. 

In sum, the Houthis would continue the war with Saudi Arabia, and the US would stay out of it. Mohammed bin Salman was politely thrown under the bus.

Meanwhile, military commanders from the US and aligned Arab states were reportedly brought together with their Israeli counterparts in Germany - a secret meeting organised by US Central Command (Centcom) to discuss the Iran war. Israel then leaked the meeting.

Sources told Israeli journalist Barak Ravid that the “private retreat” was organised by Centcom commander Admiral Brad Cooper, and attended by the military chiefs of staff of Israel, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt.

Unreliable partners

Any time Arab states secretly meet with Israeli officials, they should by now realise that it will not remain so, due to Israel’s predilection for boasting. Israel doesn’t do discreet diplomacy. It’s no secret that pro-western Arab states have been doing under-the-counter deals with “the Zionist entity” for decades.

Earlier this month, Houthi fighters launched a rapid assault from southern Hodeidah and western Taiz, capturing the Red Sea port of Mocha overnight. They then advanced to capture the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Perim Island - a strategic point overseeing the vital waterway - as Saudi-backed government troops withdrew. 

Washington is not yet ready to treat its opponents as sovereign states with legitimate interests, and to cut lasting deals with them

The fighting was bloody. Anti-Houthi National Resistance Forces reported that more than 500 of their fighters were killed and 1,500 injured. Clashes continue near Mocha and other fronts.

Saudi strikes on Yemen’s Houthi forces have been met with Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The key East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea has been hit. But Riyadh’s new Mecca defence pact allies, Turkey and Pakistan, have not come to its aid.

If not them and not Washington, then who? 

Enter Benjamin Netanyahu, who has offered military and intelligence assistance to the Gulf states. Saudi Arabia is already getting intelligence from Israel via the US on the Yemenis. Still, Riyadh does not see Israel as a reliable military partner, says Gulf analyst Andreas Krieg. “Riyadh does not want to move from dependence on Washington to dependence on an Israeli security architecture,” he told The New Arab.

Fears that Iran's Yemeni allies will close off the main route for energy and shipping through the Red Sea, on top of the semi-paralysed Strait of Hormuz, have caused further spikes in oil and diesel prices.

A senior Israeli intelligence source told Al-Monitor: “At the moment, no one has deterrence over the Houthis. Not the Americans, not us, and certainly not the Saudis. They are the dark horse that no one expected.”

Britain’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, has agreed to send military advisers to Saudi Arabia, raising fears that the UK could once again be drawn into a Saudi war on Yemen.

Trump will not intervene for Mohammed bin Salman, but he will sell billions of dollars worth of F-35s and one-tonne bombs to Riyadh. The US has just signed off on massive shipments of bombs to both Israel and Saudi Arabia. 

For Saudi Arabia, the Trump administration approved a $5bn package including 10,000 JDAM guidance kits and 10,000 bombs, split evenly between 500lb munitions and 2,000lb BLU-117s. For Israel, the $2.8bn US taxpayer-funded shipment includes 40,000 bombs - half BLU-117s and half MK-84s - and 20,000 penetrator warheads for hardened targets. It is the largest single transfer of this type of bomb to Israel in years.

The scale of these planned shipments is terrifying, as American commentator Tucker Carlson recently pointed out, dwarfing the equivalent tonnage of the Second World War US bombings of Tokyo and Hiroshima. Like those airborne atrocities, the bombs will likely be used against defenceless civilians in Gaza, Lebanon and Yemen.

How to end the war

How can this latest escalation be brought to an end? Ansar Allah, which governs more than 70 percent of Yemen’s population, insists that the war can be stopped by lifting the 12-year-old Saudi blockade on Yemen.

Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a senior Houthi spokesperson, told Sky News that Sanaa was seeking “to end the blockade and to end the aggression against Yemenis … The ball is in the Saudis’ court; it is their decision to stop this war.”

He added: “All we have done is put the equation of a blockade for a blockade”, referring to the Saudi air, land and sea cordon around Yemen, which has starved its people and caused untold suffering, leading to tens of thousands of deaths.

Saudi-Yemen conflict: The notion of an 'American saviour' is dead
Read More »

In the words of US journalist Ryan Grim, the solution to the wider conflict is simple, if unpalatable for Washington: “End the wars and treat Yemen and Iran like sovereign nations with an equal place in the world. (And also stop Israel’s attacks on southern Lebanon.) That’s it. That’s basically all they’d have to do. Just stop insisting on domination.”

Put this way, it is extraordinary how the US can disguise its actions, and those of its allies, as defensive, when in fact it has been waging a decades-long war on Iran using sanctions, assassinations, sabotage and blockades. This conflict is now longer than the Cold War.

The US empire has yet to reach a point of realism, where it can retreat from its unbridled supremacy with grace. And yet, six weeks out from the midterm elections, Trump needs to find a way to wind down the Middle East war he helped start with Netanyahu, and to tamp down record fuel prices for Americans - hence the deal with the Houthis.

Washington is not yet ready to treat its opponents as sovereign states with legitimate interests, and to cut lasting deals with them. The June memorandum with Iran looked promising, but almost immediately, Trump ripped it up.

Yet after November’s midterm elections, when Republicans are likely to be punished for Trump’s war, that may begin to change. Trillion-dollar defence bills are piling up the national debt, while global holders of US treasuries are offloading them at a worrying rate. 

After the 2028 presidential election, perhaps Trump or his successor will do as former President Richard Nixon did, and make peace with Washington’s enemies. But they would have to cut Israel loose to do it.

The views expressed in this article belong to the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial policy of Middle East Eye.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu se dramaticky vyhrotila po útocích Houthiů balistickými raketami a drony na saúdská ropná zařízení v Rijádu a Yanbu. Kolaps vládních sil v Jemenu a hrozby kontroly nad úžinou Bab al-Mandab navíc výrazně zvyšují riziko pro globální energetickou infrastrukturu a námořní trasy.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region has escalated dramatically following Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities in Riyadh and Yanbu. Furthermore, the collapse of government forces in Yemen and threats to control the Bab al-Mandab strait significantly elevate risks to global energy infrastructure and maritime routes.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další vlnu útoků a odvetných opatření v oblasti Rudého moře a Jemenu, což udrží vysokou volatilitu na trzích s ropou.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further waves of attacks and retaliatory measures in the Red Sea and Yemen are expected, maintaining high volatility in oil markets.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu se dramaticky vyhrotila po útocích Houthiů balistickými raketami a drony na saúdské hlavní město Rijád a klíčové ropné infrastruktury. Uzavření zásadního saúdského ropného potrubí a útoky na tankery v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu vyvolávají obavy z globálního energetického šoku. Spojené státy a regionální mocnosti varují před rychlou eskalací konfliktu a vyzývají občany k opatrnosti.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation has deteriorated sharply following Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh and critical oil infrastructure. The shutdown of a vital Saudi oil pipeline and tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have heightened fears of a global energy shock. The US and regional powers are warning of a rapid escalation in the conflict and urging citizens to exercise caution.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující vojenské odvetné údery a extrémní volatilitu na komoditních a akciových trzích v reakci na hrozby pro globální energetickou infrastrukturu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued military retaliatory strikes and extreme volatility in commodity and equity markets are expected in response to threats against global energy infrastructure.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Perského zálivu prudce eskaluje v důsledku opakovaných útoků Houthiů na saúdskou energetickou infrastrukturu a uzavření strategického Hormuzského průlivu. Zasažené ropné ropovody a tankery spolu s rozsáhlými vojenskými odvetami hrozí dalším ochromením globálního obchodu a dodávek energií.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf is escalating sharply due to repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and the closure of the strategic Strait of Hormuz. Struck oil pipelines and tankers, alongside extensive military retaliations, threaten further paralysis of global trade and energy supplies.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další zostření vojenských akcí v regionu Perského zálivu a Rudého moře, což udrží komoditní trhy ve stavu vysoké nervozity a volatility.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further intensification of military actions in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea region is expected, keeping commodity markets in a state of high nervousness and volatility.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu prudce eskaluje po přímých útocích Houthiů na saúdské hlavní město Rijád a klíčové ropovody. Incidenty ve Strait of Hormuz a hrozby odvetných akcí USA vůči Íránu vyvolávají obavy z širšího regionálního konfliktu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region is escalating sharply following direct Houthi attacks on the Saudi capital of Riyadh and critical oil pipelines. Incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and threats of US retaliatory actions against Iran raise concerns of a wider regional conflict.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další eskalaci napětí a možné americké vojenské údery v reakci na útoky Houthiů, což udrží ceny ropy a volatilitu na trhu na extrémně vysokých úrovních.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of tensions and potential US military strikes in response to Houthi attacks are expected, keeping oil prices and market volatility at extremely high levels.

archive.security_status_cs: Konflikt v Rudém moři a Jemenu se vyhrotil po bleskové ofenzivě Houthiů, kteří ovládli západní pobřeží a strategickou úžinu Bab al-Mandab. Útoky na saúdská ropná zařízení a metropoli Riad podtrhují selhání regionálního odstrašení a hrozbu nových výpadků dodávek energií.
archive.security_status_en: The conflict in the Red Sea and Yemen has escalated sharply following a lightning Houthi offensive seizing Yemen's west coast and the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and Riyadh highlight failing regional deterrence and the ongoing threat of major energy supply disruptions.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další diplomatické manévry a hrozbu odvetných vojenských útoků USA a spojenců v reakci na houthiské útoky na Riad. Ceny ropy a tržní volatilita zůstanou na zvýšených úrovních kvůli obavám z širší regionální války.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further diplomatic maneuvers and the threat of retaliatory military strikes by the US and allies are expected in response to Houthi attacks on Riyadh. Oil prices and market volatility will remain elevated due to fears of a broader regional war.
